title: Minimum Depth of Binary Tree
prompt:
Given the `root` of a binary tree, return its minimum depth — the number of nodes along the shortest path from the root down to the nearest leaf node.

A leaf is a node with no children. The tree is given as a level-order array where `null` marks a missing child (the standard LeetCode serialization). Your function receives this array directly; the starter code includes a helper that builds the tree from it, so you only need to implement the depth calculation.

examples.explanation: The shortest root-to-leaf path is 3 -> 9, which has 2 nodes.
The tree is a single chain with no branching, so the only leaf is at depth 5.
An empty tree has no nodes, so its minimum depth is 0.

constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [0, 10^5]
hints: This looks like Maximum Depth with min instead of max, but that substitution alone is wrong — think about why.
A node with only one child is NOT a leaf, so its minimum depth can't come from the missing (null) side, which would incorrectly report 0.
If a node has only one child, the minimum depth through that node must go through the existing child; only when both children exist do you take the min of the two subtree depths.

solution.approach: Build the tree, then recurse: an empty tree has depth 0. If a node has no children, it's a leaf with depth 1. If it has only one child, the minimum depth must route through that child (the missing side isn't a valid leaf path), so it's 1 plus that child's min depth. Only when both children exist do we take 1 plus the smaller of the two subtree depths.
